title: `md5`, `sha1`, `sha2`, `crc32`: lowercase hex of the UTF-8 bytes
verdict: `md5(s)`, `sha2(s, 256)`: hex strings of the UTF-8 bytes; `sha2` with a bad length is NULL
description: `md5`, `sha1` and `sha2(s, n)` hash the string's UTF-8 bytes (a string argument is cast to `BINARY`) and return lowercase hex `STRING`s: `md5('abc')` is `900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72`, `sha2('abc', 256)` `ba7816bf…15ad`, `md5('é')` the digest of the two bytes `c3 a9`. `sha2` takes 224, 256, 384, 512 or 0 (256); any other length gives NULL in both modes. `crc32` returns a `BIGINT`.
reference: `md5` and `sha256` (sverify's black boxes) are the lowercase hex digest of the UTF-8 bytes. Spark is native with `md5(s)` and `sha2(s, 256)`.

evidence.note: `Md5`, `Sha2`: `DigestUtils` on the bytes, hex output; `Sha2` returns NULL for other bit lengths

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
